turns.prompt_text: M2 screws, used in 3D printing with bamboo lab. Sprinters seem to be kind of expensive. Maybe I'm just not seeing the right places to buy them
turns.response_html:
It sounds like you’ve run into the classic 3D printing hardware trap—buying metric machine screws at local big-box hardware stores or in tiny individual packs is notoriously expensive. Furthermore, if you are ordering them online, the shipping can often cost more than the screws themselves.

To avoid overpaying, the best strategy is to build up a small stockpile. Here are the best and most cost-effective places to buy M2 screws for your projects:

1. Amazon (Best for starting out) Instead of looking for individual packs, search for an "M2 Socket Head Cap Screw Assortment Kit." For about $10 to $15, you can get a divided plastic organizer containing 500 to 1,000 pieces. These kits usually include a variety of common lengths (like M2x4, M2x6, M2x8, M2x12), along with the matching hex nuts and washers. It is the easiest way to make sure you always have the right size on hand.

2. Bambu Lab "Maker's Supply" (Best when ordering filament) Since you are using a Bambu Lab printer, check out the "Maker's Supply" section on their official US store. They sell M2 machine screws (in Socket, Button, and Flat head varieties) starting at around $1.00 for a 20-pack. The trick here is to never buy them alone. Just add a few packs to your cart when you are already buying enough filament to hit their free shipping threshold.

3. AliExpress (Best for dirt-cheap bulk) If you are willing to wait 1 to 3 weeks for delivery, this is the absolute cheapest option. You can buy bags of 100 or 200 screws in specific lengths for just a few dollars. Many makers buy an Amazon assortment kit first, and then use AliExpress to cheaply restock the specific sizes they use the most.

4. Bolt Depot (Best for specific US orders) If you need a large quantity of one specific length but don't want to wait for overseas shipping, Bolt Depot is a massive favorite in the 3D printing community. They sell fasteners individually or in bulk boxes, and their prices are significantly fairer than places like Lowe's or Home Depot.

A quick tip on screw types: When shopping, look specifically for Socket Head Cap Screws (SHCS) or Button Head Cap Screws (BHCS). They use a standard hex/Allen key that seats deeply into the head, making it much easier to drive them firmly into printed plastic parts without stripping them out.
